root_causes.title: Slow seller dispatch
root_causes.finding: Orders the seller took 6.0+ days to ship are late 21% of the time vs 5% when shipped within 1.8 days.

root_causes.title: Long-distance deliveries to the North-East
root_causes.finding: North-East customers get late orders 14% of the time vs 6% in São Paulo.

root_causes.title: Tight delivery promises
root_causes.finding: Orders with the shortest 25% of promises are late 9% vs 6% for the longest 25%.

root_causes.title: Business impact: late orders damage reviews
root_causes.finding: Late orders average 2.6 stars vs 4.3 on time.

forecast.note: Recent weeks are under-counted because slow orders hadn't been delivered when data was exported.

recommendations.title: Enforce a dispatch deadline for slow sellers
recommendations.description: Alert sellers whose dispatch time is in the slowest 10%; escalate after 2 days; deprioritise repeat offenders in search.
recommendations.estimate_method: Slow-dispatch orders assumed to be late at the rate of medium-dispatch orders.

recommendations.title: Add buffer days to promises for North-East routes
recommendations.description: Add 2-3 days to the promised date for high-risk routes so promises match reality.
recommendations.estimate_method: Assumes 40% of North-East late orders arrive within the added buffer (validate with delivery-day distribution).
assumptions: Slightly longer promises don't reduce conversion much

recommendations.title: Proactively handle the 10% highest-risk orders
recommendations.description: For each order in the model's top 10%: nudge the seller, upgrade carrier, and send the customer a delivery update.
evidence: Top-10% orders are late 11% vs 5% overall
recommendations.estimate_method: Assumes proactive handling prevents 30% of late deliveries among flagged orders (to be validated).

impact_simulation.note: Scenarios are estimated separately and are not additive (they overlap).

model_performance.algorithm: LightGBM + logistic regression (average of both risks)
model_performance.validation: time-based split: trained on older orders, tested on newest 20%
